question.prompt: If your average score on your first six mathematics tests was \(84\) and your average score on your first seven mathematics tests was \(85,\) then your score on the seventh test was

solutions.explanation:
An average equals the total divided by the number of tests, so multiplying the average by that number recovers the total. The first six scores add to \(6\cdot84=504\), and the first seven add to \(7\cdot85=595\).

The only score added between these two totals is the seventh score. It is therefore
\[
595-504=\boxed{91},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Recover the two totals

solutions.explanation:
Use \(85\), the final average, as the target score for each test. Since the first six average \(84\), their total is
\[
6(85-84)=6
\]
points below the total of six scores of \(85\). To make all seven tests average \(85\), the seventh score must supply those missing \(6\) points in addition to its own \(85\). Thus it is \(85+6=\boxed{91}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Balance around 85
